Idea: Add right-click menu when clicking in 'blank space' of sidebar. One item: 
Customize Sidebar

@Yulia Popova - Can you provide some context around this exploration for a right-click menu for vertical tabs? The note suggests that there's a possibility we can't have the same right click menu for tabs, if they're positioned vertically. Was this an engineering consideration? Something you were thinking we should explore from a UX perspective?

@Katie Lower and @Yulia Popova - while the consistency is important for a few reasons, there is some wiggle room here because we're introducing new component with new orientation and new set of functionality for tabs. 

Users aren't likely to have muscle memory to, for instance, reopen the closed tab with the context menu. Plus, the options that will be included for pinned tabs too are nearly the same, they appear in the same order (i.e to reload the tab a keyboard user would need to press "Down" arrow twice in both cases) and cover the basic functionality. 

And for the pinned tabs specifically, I think removing the "Close tab" option would be beneficial for users with cognitive difficulties because, well, pinned tabs are always open (but could be unpinned instead to remove it from the toolbar).

I think the offered variation (small number of unrelated menu items is skipped for pinned tabs) would be acceptable. We probably don't want to only allow to leave 2 options for pinned tabs while unpinned ones have 11, but this is not what's been considered anyway :)

Thank you for reaching out about it!

@Emanuela Damiani Not ideal, but I think we can have something like this for the expanded state. I personally think that it would be okay if we had a different representation of pinned tabs in the expanded view for horizontal tab setup and for vertical tabs setup. Thinking about these scenarios helped me understand that pinned tabs and tools should not be mixed. Their design, interaction, and active states are different. But curious to hear your thoughts as well.
@Katie Lower what do you think about adding this info to each subcategory that can be pinned?

@Yulia Popova and @Eric Pang - Would love your review and crit of these various sidebar menu options. And also feedback on if you think the hypothesis holds... and whether we can validate it.

* tabs/tasks aside for later, 
* deliveries (Fedex, USPS, UPS).
The group name could be auto-suggested based on the pages keywords or themes extraction.
@Yulia Popova I need to install SF Pro, it keeps disappearing from available fonts for me. I think a fitting generalized prompt could be "Add this URL as a task".
@Yulia Popova I was not sure what this button would do and wondered if it could be a "stacking" tab group action button, where you can drag tabs to separate them from your whole list of open tabs.

@Yulia Popova noting that for the purposes of the prototype we decided to add (from top to bottom:
* recently closed tabs/history (one icon),
* bookmarks,
* downloads,
* optional - profile - the purpose of this one is to test what do users expect there.
@Yulia Popova added another example of a potential realistic prompt that we can try out

Implicit user intent: we're guessing they will find this useful
Agent (conversational) AI goes here in this approach
lol
@Ania Safko I think you mean horizontal tab

@Yulia Popova I think there are (at least) two potential approaches to Home:
* everything that's important and relevant to the current page (this begs a question on what's the role of the awesome bar then - just search and retrieval? Or are we now showing some page actions in the awesome bar, while others - in the sidebar?), 
* AI-powered edge-copilot like experience that tries to bring in all sorts of stuff an LLM can do to help users be more productive, return to the relevant tasks, etc. I think Edge does it terribly right now, tbh. So to provide value, we'll need to do way more than throwing random prompts on the page as Edge does. 
* some mixture of both approaches.
We'll also need to give users a segmentation survey at some point, to understand what group they belong to.
Spoke with Jon and it seems that we might want to start with a simpler, async version of this (e.g., create a figjam/miro and provide instructions on how to participate).
Think about what existing threads should be notified about this post once it goes live.

Some of these tools (chatgpt, notes, any sidebar-ready extensions like todoist would occupy the column view. So column view would exist in some sense, but it's a valid question whether "home" is actually useful in this approach.

Let's perhaps test two different alternatives? The known challenge with the current pinned tabs is they are not easily discoverable as functionality, but users find a lot of value in them (usage is low, but consistent). What do you think?
Existing sidebar button: no longer necessary (since the open tabs button already serves the same purpose), we removed it from the prototype

Toolbar action button: toggles horizontal tabs (and bookmarks toolbar ideally) on and off
Purpose: let prototype testers get back to full functionality of the tab strip if necessary
Open tabs button: toggles the column view of the sidebar on and off
I think download is a more common icon to be surfaced as history and synced tabs.
Maybe we add search at the top and show more narrow selection by default? A long list of items feels overwhelming.
I am wondering if there is a difference between how users add pinned tab and shortcuts to web apps or other widgets? And if we should have intentionally different ways to do it.
I think we should be consistent in the way we use headers for all cards. Testing a version with headers inside of cards.
I think we should be consistent in the way we use headers for all cards. Testing a version with headers outside of cards.

This separator is possible a little too "modest" and not noticeable separator for this approach, but I think we can have display both pinned and regular tabs vertically in this case, if we show the separation a little clearer.

Think about how we can avoid presenting an extra hierarchy layer here or, if impossible, what should be the order of items here and how to divide them into logical sections, e.g. "destinations" (bookmarks, shopping, extensions) and application-level actions (customize settings, appearance, etc).

Perhaps, in this approach, items in the URL bar are all actionable, e.g.,:
* bookmarking, 
* copying the url, 
* sharing the url,
* "sideviewing" the tab, 
* making a screenshot
While the toolbar houses "actionable" add-ons - ones that perform actions on a page rather than provide information about it.

@Emanuela Damiani @Yulia Popova perhaps the best approach/default view is somewhere in the synthesis of approach 1 and 2: I feel like vertical tabs view would be greatly enhanced if calendar "widget" with the upcoming meetings was sitting "on top" of the vertical tabs.

Perhaps we use: 
* on-hover states - to expose most frequently used or important information, 
* on-click - open the full list of items in a column view (if such a list exists)?

I have used the term "destinations" for brevity to identify all the different things in this lower bottom area. @Emanuela Damiani @Yulia Popova not attached to either terms, just wanted a faster way to refer to these.

I have used the term "shortcuts" for the pinned tabs for brevity for now. 
@Emanuela Damiani @Yulia Popova

@Eric Pang @Yulia Popova @Emanuela Damiani at a risk of trying to test too much simultaneously, I think we'll have to deal with the problem of vertical stacking (tab bar, awesome bar, bookmarks bar, various website specific bars) pretty early. What do you think about attempting to come up with a conceptual framework that will allow us to separate actions (e.g. save something for later, via Pocket or otherwise) that likely make sense in the toolbar from static entry points (e.g., hamburger menu) that might be better placed towards the bottom of the vertical bar?

@Eric Pang @Yulia Popova @Emanuela Damiani I've been thinking about the dichotomy of recently closed tabs/history resulting in two icons leading users to essentially the same location. What do you think about changing the pattern a bit: keeping the history icon, but displaying recently closed tabs on hover in a scrollable dialog?

@Eric Pang @Yulia Popova @Emanuela Damiani Hi folks! Displaying the Window 1 label when only one window is in use (the vastest majority of cases) feels extraneous as it takes a good deal of vertical space. What do you think about displaying the label only if more than one window is open?
